arxiv-1601-00251.title: A high-finesse Fabry-Perot cavity with a frequency-doubled green laser for precision Compton polarimetry at Jefferson Lab Journal: Nuc. Instr. and Meth. A
arxiv-1601-00251.creator: A. Rakhman, M. Hafez, S. Nanda, F. Benmokhtar, A. Camsonne, G.D. Cates, M.M. Dalton, G.B. Franklin, M. Friend, R.W. Michaels, V. Nelyubin, D.S. Parno, K.D. Paschke, B.P. Quinn, P.A. Souder, W.A. Tobias
arxiv-1601-00251.description: Abstract A high-finesse Fabry-Perot cavity with a frequency-doubled continuous wave green laser (532 nm) has been built and installed in Hall A of Jefferson Lab for high precision Compton polarimetry. The infrared (1064 nm) beam from a ytterbium-doped fiber amplifier seeded by a Nd:YAG nonplanar ring oscillator laser is frequency doubled in a single-pass periodically poled MgO:LiNbO 3 crystal.

arxiv-2207-07662.title: Superradiance in Stars: Non-equilibrium approach to damping of fields in stellar media
arxiv-2207-07662.creator: F. Chadha-Day, B. Garbrecht, J. I. McDonald
arxiv-2207-07662.description: Abstract Superradiance in black holes is well-understood but a general treatment for superradiance in stars has until now been lacking. This is surprising given the ease with which we can observe isolated neutron stars and the array of signatures which would result from stellar superradiance.

arxiv-2208-06086.title: On fillings of contact links of quotient singularities
arxiv-2208-06086.creator: Zhengyi Zhou
arxiv-2208-06086.description: Abstract . We study several aspects of fillings for links of general isolated quotient singularities using Floer theory, including co-fillings, Weinstein fillings, strong fillings, exact fillings and exact orbifold fillings, focusing on the non-existence of exact fillings of contact links of isolated terminal quotient singularities.

arxiv-2504-01398.title: Cause or Trigger? From Philosophy to Causal Modeling
arxiv-2504-01398.creator: Kateřina Hlaváčková-Schindler katerina.schindlerova@univie.ac.at, Rainer Wößrainer.woess@univie.ac.at, Vera Pecorino pecov1800@gmail.com, Philip Schindler a12315546@unet.univie.ac.at
arxiv-2504-01398.description: Abstract Not much has been written about the role of triggers in the literature on causal reasoning, causal modeling, or philosophy. In this paper, we focus on describing triggers and causes in the metaphysical sense and on characterizations that differentiate them from each other. We carry out a philosophical analysis of these differences.

arxiv-2512-12984.title: VoroLight : Learning Quality Volumetric Voronoi Meshes from General Inputs
arxiv-2512-12984.creator: Jiayin Lu, Ying Jiang, Yin Yang, Chenfanfu Jiang
arxiv-2512-12984.description: Abstract We present VoroLight , a differentiable framework for 3D shape reconstruction based on Voronoi meshing. Our approach generates smooth, watertight surfaces and topologically consistent volumetric meshes directly from diverse inputs, including images, implicit shape level-set fields, point clouds and meshes.

arxiv-2601-18303.title: Dicey Games: Shared Sources of Randomness in Distributed Systems DOI: XXXXXXX.XXXXXXX ISBN: 978-1-4503-XXXX-X/2018/06 CCS: Theory of computation Probabilistic computation CCS: Mathematics of computing Distribution functions CCS: Theory of computation Random network models
arxiv-2601-18303.creator: Léonard Brice, Thomas A. Henzinger, K. S. Thejaswini
arxiv-2601-18303.description: A 2026 arXiv research paper by Léonard Brice, Thomas A. Henzinger, K. S. Thejaswini. Consider a 4-player version of Matching Pennies where a team of three players competes against the Devil. Each player simultaneously says “Heads” or “Tails”. The team wins if all four choices match; otherwise the Devil wins. If all team players randomise independently, they win with probability 1 / 8 1/8 ; if all players share a common source of randomness, they win with probability 1 / 2 1/2 .

pmc-10711016.title: Differential molecular profiles and associated functionalities characterize connective tissue grafts obtained at different locations and depths in the human palate
pmc-10711016.creator: Maria B Asparuhova, Xiaoqing Song, Dominic Riedwyl, Geert van Geest, Dieter D Bosshardt, Anton Sculean
pmc-10711016.description: The present study aimed to assess the molecular profiles of subepithelial connective tissue grafts (CTGs) obtained at different locations and depths in the human palate. Sixty-four CTGs belonging to anterior deep (AD), anterior superficial (AS), posterior deep (PD), and posterior superficial (PS) groups were subjected to RNA-Sequencing and their transcriptomes were analyzed computationally.

pmc-10752088.title: Long-Term Outcomes of Infinity Total Ankle Arthroplasty Compared to Ankle Arthrodesis
pmc-10752088.creator: Madeleine Willegger, Andrea Veljkovic, Alastair Younger, Kevin Wing, Murray Penner
pmc-10752088.description: Category:Ankle Arthritis; AnkleIntroduction/Purpose:End-stage ankle arthritis causes severe pain and disability. The most common treatment has been ankle arthrodesis (AA) with proven long-term results. However, total ankle arthroplasty (TAA) has become a viable option to preserve ankle joint motion, relieve pain and shield adjacent joints.

pmc-11399736.title: Self-management support from health care providers in Shared Medical Appointments: Didactic techniques, peer learning, group dynamics and motivation
pmc-11399736.creator: Anna H.C. Tsiamparlis-Wildeboer, Esther I. Feijen-De Jong, Elke Tichelman, Ank de Jonge, Fedde Scheele
pmc-11399736.description: ObjectiveWe investigated the support of self-management by health care providers (HCP) in prenatal Shared Medical Appointments (SMA).Methodson an topic list, semi-structured interviews were conducted. HCP who provided prenatal care in SMA in the last five years were recruited. Thematic analysis was used.ResultsWe conducted 15 interviews. Four research themes were defined: didactic techniques, peer learning, motivation and the health care providers.

pmc-11543162.title: Management of velopharyngeal insufficiency by a new modification of sphincter pharyngoplasty technique in cleft palate patients, clinical and radiographical prospective study
pmc-11543162.creator: Jafar Hamdy, Hikmat Yacoub
pmc-11543162.description: Background:This study was designed to investigate the effectiveness and outcome of a new modification of the sphincter pharyngoplasty technique in the treatment of velopharyngeal insufficiency patients, with the determination of a specific dimension of velopharyngeal port and velum length of no hypernasality, snoring, and nasal regurgitation potential.

pmc-11616635.title: Rough Edges, Meticulous Attention
pmc-11616635.creator: Byron Breedlove
pmc-11616635.description: tomb walls were first plastered with a thick mixture of mud and straw, followed by a thinner, smooth layer suitable for painting. According to the British Museum, a team of artists created the images, initially sketching outlines for each scene, then adding details, using for pigments a range of natural materials, including soot and various ground stones and minerals.

pmc-11620018.title: Impaired processing of spatiotemporal visual attention engagement deficits in Chinese children with developmental dyslexia
pmc-11620018.creator: Baojun Duan, Xiaoling Tang, Datao Wang, Yanjun Zhang, Guihua An, Huan Wang, Aibao Zhou
pmc-11620018.description: Emerging evidence suggests that visuospatial attention plays an important role in reading among Chinese children with dyslexia. Additionally, numerous studies have shown that Chinese children with dyslexia have deficits in their visuospatial attention orienting; however, the visual attention engagement deficits in Chinese children with dyslexia remain unclear.

pmc-11642472.title: Current and Evolving Biomarkers in the Diagnosis and Management of Testicular Germ Cell Tumors
pmc-11642472.creator: Jennifer Sykes, Alain Kaldany, Thomas L. Jang
pmc-11642472.description: Testicular cancer is the most common cancer among young adult men and has favorable outcomes, with survival rates approaching 99% and over 80% for those with early and advanced stage disease, respectively. Biomarkers play a critical role in the diagnosis, pre-treatment risk stratification, surveillance, and assessment of post-treatment disease response in these men.

pmc-11657153.title: Mosquito breeding water parameters are important determinants for Microsporidia MB in the aquatic stages of Anopheles species
pmc-11657153.creator: Esinam A. Akorli, Nana Efua Andoh, Richardson K. Egyirifa, Christopher Dorcoo, Sampson Otoo, Seraphim N. A. Tetteh, Reuben Mwimson Pul, Derrick B. Sackitey, Stephen K. D. Oware, Samuel K. Dadzie, Jewelna Akorli
pmc-11657153.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2024). BackgroundMicrosporidia MB disrupts Plasmodium development in Anopheles mosquitoes, making it a possible biocontrol tool for malaria. As a tool for vector/disease control, its ecological distribution and the factors that determine their occurrence must be defined.

pmc-11699465.title: Nuclear transmembrane protein 199 promotes immune escapes by up-regulating programmed death ligand 1
pmc-11699465.creator: Wulin You, Hue Luu, Meili Li, Zhiyu Chen, Fangchao Li, Yanfei Zhang, Mingsheng Cai, Tong-chuan He, Jingjing Li
pmc-11699465.description: SummaryThe function of transmembrane protein 199 (TMEM199) in cancer development has rarely been studied thus far. We report the nuclear localization of the TMEM199 protein and further analyzed the truncated fractions that mediate its nuclear localization. Cut&Tag assay globally explores the nuclear-located TMEM199 functions and tests its influence on the immune checkpoint PD-L1 in vitro and in vivo.

pmc-12358071.title: MicroRNA profiles of four induced pluripotent stem cell lines derived from distinct tissues
pmc-12358071.creator: Kongtana Trakarnsanga, Nutchavadee Vorasan, Nutnicha Tantarungsee, Methichit Wattanapanitch, Chinnavuth Vatanashevanopakorn, Bhoom Suktitipat, Chanatip Metheetrairut
pmc-12358071.description: ObjectiveInduced pluripotent stem cells (iPSCs) are generated from a vast number of adult cell types. While they all acquired embryonic stem cell (ESC)-like properties during reprogramming, differences in certain characteristics, including differentiation potential, remained. These differences are hypothesized to be due to epigenetic memory or individual genetic background.

pmc-12397214.title: Modeling resource consumption in the US air transportation system via minimum-cost percolation
pmc-12397214.creator: Minsuk Kim, C Tyler Diggans, Filippo Radicchi
pmc-12397214.description: Percolation theory has been proven useful to study the robustness of supply-and-demand networks (SDNs) such as transportation and communication infrastructures. Here, we show that it can also be leveraged to understand how resources of SDNs are utilized, and eventually depleted. We introduce a model where rational agents consume network’s edges along demanded minimum-cost paths.

pmc-12578453.title: Canada’s youth are part of the opioid crisis and need treatment
pmc-12578453.creator: Shannon Charlebois, Shawn Kelly
pmc-12578453.description: id supply occur in youth. In British Columbia, unregulated drug toxicity became the leading cause of death among 15- to 18-year-olds in 2021.2 The problem runs deeper than the toxic supply. Early-onset initiation and escalation of opioid use among youth is being overlooked.

pmc-12586513.title: Efficient energy management of a low-voltage AC microgrid with renewable and energy storage integration using nonlinear control
pmc-12586513.creator: Karim El Mezdi, Abdelmounime El Magri, Aziz Watil, Ilyass El Myasse, Nabil El Aadouli, Pankaj Kumar
pmc-12586513.description: This paper proposes an enhanced nonlinear control strategy combined with efficient energy flow management for a low-voltage AC microgrid integrating a wind turbine, a photovoltaic system, and a battery energy storage unit. The microgrid operates in a grid-connected configuration, aiming to optimize energy generation, storage, and consumption.

pmc-13222731.title: Bouveret Syndrome: A Systematic Review of Clinical Factors Associated With Surgical Management
pmc-13222731.creator: Maximus S Reese, Salma Alkhatib, Philip J Haynos, Garret Rymer, Noor Chughtai, Jared Nichols
pmc-13222731.description: Bouveret syndrome is a rare form of gallstone ileus characterized by the formation of a cholecystoenteric fistula and subsequent gallstone migration into the gastrointestinal tract, resulting in gastric outlet obstruction. Diagnostic criteria consist of clinical evidence (persistent non-bilious vomiting, nausea, epigastric pain) paired with imaging (CT abdomen showing ectopic gallstone, gastric outlet obstruction, cholecystoenteric fistula) and endoscopy.

pmc-13243820.title: Experiences of functional recovery after polytrauma in a private Johannesburg healthcare setting: Patients’ perspectives
pmc-13243820.creator: Mughammad A. Reis, Monique M. Keller, Heleen van Aswegen
pmc-13243820.description: BackgroundThe prevalence of polytrauma is increasing globally and in South Africa, contributing to the reported rates of disability. Early physiotherapy intervention in the acute care setting reduces the risk of complications and facilitates functional recovery of patients who sustained polytrauma injuries.

pmc-13258741.title: A Retrospective Analysis of Distal Shoe Space Maintainers Placed in a Specialised Paediatric Dental Clinic
pmc-13258741.creator: Rakan Hamad, Julian Schmoeckel, Christian H. Splieth, Maria Abdin
pmc-13258741.description: Background: Space management after the premature extraction of second primary molars remains a challenge. Distal Shoe space maintainers (DSSMs) have been recommended after such extraction before the eruption of first permanent molars (FPMs) to prevent space loss and subsequent complications. There is lack of evidence for their clinical use and possible complications after their insertion.
